title: Trump compares his nuclear knowledge with Obama’s at a 2016 rally
description_short: Trump compares his nuclear knowledge with Obama’s at a 2016 rally
description_medium: At an April 2, 2016 campaign appearance in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, Donald Trump criticized President Barack Obama and said, “I know more about nuclear than he’ll ever know.” The report documents a campaign boast and its comparison target; it does not support the later claim that Trump said he knew more than anyone or assess his nuclear-policy expertise.
description_long: Donald Trump made this remark at a campaign appearance in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, on April 2, 2016. NBC News described it as his third and final campaign stop that Saturday. The Wisconsin primary was scheduled for Tuesday, and the article reported that Trump was trailing Ted Cruz by double digits. Trump had emphasized jobs and the economy for most of the day before turning to foreign policy at the rallies. In Eau Claire, he criticized President Barack Obama, whom NBC said had challenged Trump’s foreign and nuclear policy earlier in the week. Trump called Obama “incompetent” and, responding to the president’s Friday comments, said: “I know more about nuclear than he’ll ever know. I know what’s right and wrong.” He then turned to Japan, South Korea, and North Korea. The report identifies Obama as the comparison target. It documents what Trump said, but does not test his expertise, establish that he knew more than anyone, or substantiate the claim that he bypassed expert advice because of this boast.

sources.title: Donald Trump Woos Wisconsin With Jobs-and-Economy Pitch
sources.support_note: NBC News reports the April 2, 2016 Eau Claire campaign appearance as Trump’s third and final Wisconsin campaign stop that Saturday; says he trailed Ted Cruz by double digits before Tuesday’s primary; describes his jobs-and-economy pitch and foreign-policy turn; quotes Trump’s response to President Obama’s comments and his subsequent pivot to Japan, South Korea, and North Korea. The reported nuclear comparison is to Obama.
sources.uncertainty: The report verifies the reported utterance and context, not the truth of Trump’s boast, a comparative assessment of expertise, the claim that he knew more than anyone, or a causal claim about policy or expert advice. It does not support the previous long-description detail naming Memorial High School, which was removed.

The report supplies the rally and campaign context included in the expanded long description.
